sanskrit_shloka:
जनक उवाच ॥
कायकृत्यासहः पूर्वं ततो वाग्विस्तरासहः ।
अथ चिन्तासहस्तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥ १२-१॥
translation: Janaka said: At first I could not bear the activities of the body; then the elaboration of speech; at last, even thoughts themselves became intolerable. Thus have I become established in my true nature.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Janaka said: At first I could not bear the activities of the body; then the elaboration of speech; at last, even thoughts themselves became intolerable. Thus have I become established in my true nature.

commentary_faqs.question: Why does Janaka say even meditation is a distraction?
commentary_faqs.answer: Janaka realizes that the effort to meditate implies a dualistic struggle between a meditator and an object, whereas the Self is already ever-present and requires no effort to be.

commentary_faqs.question: What does being established in one's true nature mean?
commentary_faqs.answer: It refers to Swarupa-Avastha, a state where the mind stops seeking or rejecting and rests in the pure, non-dual consciousness of the Self without any external or internal movement.

translation: Seeing the absence of attachment in sense objects such as sound, and recognizing that the Self is not an object of sight, my heart became free from distraction and gathered into stillness. Thus have I become established in my true nature.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Seeing the absence of attachment in sense objects such as sound, and recognizing that the Self is not an object of sight, my heart became free from distraction and gathered into stillness. Thus have I become established in my true nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
समाध्यासादिविक्षिप्तौ व्यवहारः समाधये ।
एवं विलोक्य नियममेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥ १२-३॥ ।
translation: Seeing that activity gives rise to distraction and that samādhi depends on discipline and rule, I abandoned even the effort to concentrate. Thus have I become established in my true nature.

translations.author: English Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
हेयोपादेयविरहाद् एवं हर्षविषादयोः ।
अभावादद्य हे ब्रह्मन्न् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥ १२-४॥
translation: O Brahman, having relinquished both what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted, and seeing the absence of joy and sorrow alike, today I am thus established in my true nature.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: O Brahman, having relinquished both what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted, and seeing the absence of joy and sorrow alike, today I am thus established in my true nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
आश्रमानाश्रमं ध्यानं चित्तस्वीकृतवर्जनम् ।
विकल्पं मम वीक्ष्यैतैरेवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥ १२-५॥
translation: Seeing that the stages of life and their absence, meditation, and the mind’s acceptance and rejection are but imaginations, I have thus become established in my true nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
अचिन्त्यं चिन्त्यमानोऽपि चिन्तारूपं भजत्यसौ ।
त्यक्त्वा तद्भावनं तस्माद् एवमेवाहमास्थितः ॥ १२-७॥
translation: Even when the inconceivable is thought upon, it assumes the form of thought. Therefore, abandoning such contemplation, I have thus become established in my true nature.

sanskrit_shloka:
एवमेव कृतं येन स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ।
एवमेव स्वभावो यः स कृतार्थो भवेदसौ ॥ १२-८॥
translation: One who acts in this way becomes fulfilled. One whose very nature is this way becomes fulfilled.
